coauthors.name: Javier Garcia Gilabert
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Works on MT with LLMs (PLUME, MT-LENS, SalamandraTA WMT25). Reviewed arXiv record: machine translation quality/evaluation and multilingual model training only, no work on culture, cultural or moral values, cross-cultural differences, cultural bias or value alignment. Rejected under the strict gate as generic multilingual NLP.

coauthors.name: Carlos Escolano
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Co-author on 'The power of Prompts: Evaluating and Mitigating Gender Bias in MT with LLMs' and 'Gender Bias in Multilingual Neural Machine Translation: The Architecture Matters'. This is gender bias in translation with no cultural-values dimension, which the gate explicitly excludes; remaining work is MT architecture and evaluation.

coauthors.name: Aleix Sant Savall
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Papers include gender bias in MT, SpeechAlign, federated multilingual LLMs, and 'EuroAlpaca: Task-Preserving Localisation of Instruction Data for European Languages'. EuroAlpaca is the closest candidate but its abstract frames localisation purely as preserving task-critical constraints: 'our pipeline applies field-wise MT while preserving task-critical content or reconstructs a task-equivalent target-language instance' - task semantics, not cultural or value localization. Rejected.

coauthors.name: Francesca De Luca Fornaciari
coauthors.relevance_evidence: arXiv record covers gender bias in MT with LLMs, idiom detection with conversational LLMs, ACADATA and SalamandraTA. Idiom detection is figurative-language understanding, not cultural values; gender bias has no cultural dimension per the gate. Rejected.

coauthors.name: Xixian Liao
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Co-author of 'Challenges and Recommendations for LLM-as-a-Judge in Multilingual Settings and for Low-Resource Languages' and 'The Impact of Familiarity on Naming Variation: A Study on Object Naming in Mandarin Chinese'. The judge paper is about evaluation reliability - 'inconsistent evaluation outcomes, a tendency to overtrust LLM judgments in multilingual settings' - a multilingual/low-resource evaluation concern with no cultural-values framing. Rejected.

coauthors.name: Maite Melero
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Senior BSC/AINA author; arXiv record is Catalan and multilingual language resources, MT evaluation, gender bias in MT and idiom detection. No work on culture, moral values, cultural bias or value alignment in LLMs. Rejected as generic multilingual NLP.

coauthors.name: Severino Da Dalt
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Papers: Salamandra Technical Report, SalamandraTA WMT25, MrBERT multilingual encoders. Multilingual model building only; no cultural or values component. Rejected.
